purpose: machine-readable ontology for identifying and appraising natural-language arguments—distinguishing arguments from non-arguments, extracting premises/conclusions, classifying and appraising the three inference types, and diagnosing informal fallacies and cognitive biases including when an apparent fallacy is a reasonable defeasible move—as a subdomain node of argumentation and critical reasoning for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: Informal Logic & Fallacies is modeled as a subdomain of argumentation and critical reasoning.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable diagnostic or appraisal work units (how to detect, name, and judge), not lists of fallacies.
No observed dataset or experimental evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Scope follows Walton (2008), Copi/Cohen/McMahon (2016), Hamblin (1970), and Kahneman (2011) on fallacies, inference, and reasoning biases.
Fallacy diagnosis is dialectical and defeasible: an apparent fallacy may be a reasonable presumptive move depending on dialogue type and answered critical questions.
exclusions: Formal proof theory, model theory, and symbolic-logic metatheory beyond recognizing valid/invalid argument forms.
Rhetoric and persuasion technique design that does not bear on argument appraisal.
Empirical psychology experiments measuring bias prevalence (no observed data supplied).
Domain-specific subject-matter truth of premises beyond their logical role.

competency_questions.question: Given a natural-language passage, is it an argument and what are its premises and conclusion?
How is the argument standardized and which unstated premises must be charitably supplied?
Is the argument deductive, inductive, or abductive, and which appraisal standard applies?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INFERENCE_TYPE_CLASS routes to the matching standard

competency_questions.question: Is a deductive argument valid and sound, and which named form or formal fallacy does it instantiate?
How strong/cogent is an inductive or abductive argument given its evidence and rivals?
When is an apparent fallacy actually a reasonable defeasible move under its argumentation scheme?
To which informal-fallacy category (relevance, ambiguity, presumption) does a defect belong?
Is a personal or source-directed move a fallacious relevance failure or a legitimate credibility challenge?
Does a term shift sense or a sentence carry structural ambiguity across the argument?
Which presumption fallacy (false dilemma, begging the question, hasty generalization, slippery slope) is present?
Has the opponent's position been distorted (straw man) rather than addressed at its strongest?
Before issuing a fallacy verdict, was the strongest faithful reading evaluated under the principle of charity?
Do cognitive biases (confirmation, motivated reasoning, anchoring, availability) corrupt the reasoning process?

glossary.definition: a set of premises offered in support of a conclusion
an argument with an unstated but intended premise or conclusion
property of a deductive argument where true premises guarantee a true conclusion
a valid deductive argument all of whose premises are true
degree to which an inductive argument's premises make its conclusion probable
a strong inductive argument with true premises
inference to the best explanation among competing hypotheses
a presumptively warranted inference that can be defeated by new information or unanswered critical questions
an argument that is psychologically persuasive but logically defective for reasons of content or context, not form
a fallacy in which a key term shifts meaning between premises
an argument whose premise presupposes or restates its conclusion
refuting a distorted, weaker version of an opponent's actual position
interpreting an argument in its strongest faithful form before evaluating it
the tendency to seek and weight evidence that supports a prior belief

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established informal-logic and reasoning literature (e.g., Walton 2008; Copi, Cohen & McMahon 2016; Hamblin 1970; Kahneman 2011) and critical-thinking practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Decide whether a passage actually advances an argument (premises offered for a conclusion) rather than an explanation, description, narration, conditional, or report.
contradictors: rhetorician who treats all persuasion as argument

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when context reframes a passage from report to inferential claim

pros.claim: prevents wasting fallacy analysis on passages that make no inferential claim
pros.example: an explanation of why a bridge fell is not an argument that it fell

cons.claim: misclassification cascades: treating an explanation as an argument invents nonexistent fallacies
cons.example: reading a conditional 'if p then q' as an asserted inference

failure_modes: explanation mistaken for argument
rhetorical question read as a premise
acceptance_tests: passage contains at least one premise offered in support of a conclusion
non-inferential passages are explicitly excluded

nodes.definition: Identify the conclusion and its supporting premises using indicator words, the inference-to question, and context, separating stated from unstated content.
contradictors: reader who fixes the conclusion before reading the premises

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an alternative reading relocates the main conclusion

pros.claim: correct premise/conclusion mapping is the substrate for every later appraisal
pros.example: 'therefore' marks the conclusion; 'because' marks a premise

cons.claim: misidentifying the main conclusion mis-frames the whole evaluation
cons.example: treating an intermediate conclusion as the final one

failure_modes: sub-conclusion mistaken for main conclusion
missing implicit conclusion
acceptance_tests: each premise and the conclusion are explicitly labeled
indicator words reconciled with the inference-to test

nodes.definition: Rewrite the argument in standard form, supply missing but intended premises (enthymemes) under the principle of charity, and remove rhetorical padding.
contradictors: uncharitable critic who adds premises that weaken the case

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the charitable reconstruction is contested as a misreading

pros.claim: explicit enthymeme supply exposes the real load-bearing assumption
pros.example: 'Socrates is mortal because he is a man' supplies 'all men are mortal'

cons.claim: supplying an unintended premise creates a straw or steel man not under test
cons.example: adding a false universal the author never assumed

failure_modes: over-charitable repair changes the thesis
padding retained as if it were a premise
acceptance_tests: every supplied premise is justified by author intent or context
standard form preserves the original conclusion

nodes.definition: Classify the argument's intended inference as deductive, inductive, or abductive so the correct appraisal standard is applied.
contradictors: monist who appraises all arguments by deductive validity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the arguer's intended standard (necessity vs probability) is reinterpreted

pros.claim: selecting the right standard prevents category-error appraisals
pros.example: judging an inductive generalization 'invalid' is a category error

cons.claim: intended type can be ambiguous in natural language
cons.example: 'must' may signal logical necessity or mere emphasis

failure_modes: inductive argument held to deductive validity
abduction mistaken for affirming the consequent
acceptance_tests: inference type stated with the cue that fixes it
chosen appraisal standard matches the type

nodes.definition: Appraise deductive arguments for validity (impossible for premises true and conclusion false) and soundness (valid plus true premises).
contradictors: relativist who denies objective validity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a hidden premise turns an invalid form valid or vice versa

pros.claim: validity is truth-preserving and form-decidable independent of content
pros.example: modus ponens guarantees the conclusion if the premises hold

cons.claim: a valid argument can still be unsound with a false premise
cons.example: valid but rests on a false universal premise

failure_modes: validity conflated with truth of the conclusion
soundness asserted without checking premise truth
acceptance_tests: a counterexample is sought for any claimed-valid form
validity and soundness verdicts are stated separately

nodes.definition: Recognize common valid forms (modus ponens, modus tollens, hypothetical/disjunctive syllogism) and their formal-fallacy look-alikes (affirming the consequent, denying the antecedent).
contradictors: intuition-only reasoner who skips form-checking

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when surface phrasing hides the underlying conditional form

pros.claim: pattern-matching to named forms makes formal fallacies fast to flag
pros.example: 'if p then q; q; so p' is affirming the consequent

cons.claim: natural-language conditionals can mask the true logical form
cons.example: 'only if' and 'unless' invert the antecedent/consequent

failure_modes: affirming the consequent accepted as valid
denying the antecedent missed
acceptance_tests: each conditional argument is matched to a named form
invalid forms produce an explicit counterexample

nodes.definition: Appraise inductive arguments for strength (premises make the conclusion probable) and cogency (strong plus true premises), judging sample, analogy, and statistical support.
contradictors: deductivist who dismisses non-demonstrative support

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new evidence raises or lowers the conclusion's probability

pros.claim: degree-based appraisal fits real-world non-demonstrative reasoning
pros.example: a large representative sample yields a strong generalization

cons.claim: strength is defeasible and sensitive to total evidence
cons.example: a strong inference collapses when a counter-instance appears

failure_modes: strength treated as all-or-nothing
ignoring base rates or sample bias
acceptance_tests: strength is rated on the evidence offered, not certainty
relevant total evidence is considered

nodes.definition: Appraise inference to the best explanation by comparing candidate hypotheses on explanatory virtues (scope, simplicity, consilience, testability) against rivals.
contradictors: naive falsificationist who rejects explanatory inference

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a previously unconsidered rival hypothesis is introduced

pros.claim: explicit rival comparison blocks 'only explanation I thought of' errors
pros.example: preferring the hypothesis with greatest consilience and fewest assumptions

cons.claim: best of a bad set is still weak; virtues can conflict
cons.example: simplest explanation may have the least scope

failure_modes: unique-explanation assumed without ruling out rivals
explanatory virtues applied selectively
acceptance_tests: at least one rival hypothesis is explicitly compared
the chosen hypothesis dominates rivals on stated virtues

nodes.definition: Decide whether an apparent fallacy is actually a reasonable defeasible move (presumptive, context-licensed) rather than an error, using argumentation-scheme critical questions.
contradictors: fallacy-list absolutist who labels by form alone

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the dialogue type or burden of proof is reinterpreted

pros.claim: prevents over-diagnosis: many 'fallacies' are legitimate presumptive inferences
pros.example: an appeal to a qualified expert is reasonable unless critical questions fail

cons.claim: the reasonable/fallacious line is context-sensitive and contestable
cons.example: the same slope argument is sound with evidence, fallacious without

failure_modes: legitimate presumptive inference labeled a fallacy
fallacy excused by appeal to context without checking critical questions
acceptance_tests: the relevant argumentation scheme and its critical questions are identified
verdict turns on whether critical questions are answered, not form alone

nodes.definition: Route a flagged defect to the correct informal-fallacy category (relevance, ambiguity, presumption) before naming the specific fallacy.
contradictors: pundit who name-drops fallacies without categorizing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a defect fits multiple categories and routing is contested

pros.claim: category-first routing reduces mislabeling and overlapping diagnoses
pros.example: irrelevant attack -> relevance; shifting word sense -> ambiguity

cons.claim: some fallacies straddle categories
cons.example: equivocation can also create a relevance failure

failure_modes: wrong category routes to the wrong critical questions
fallacy named before category fixed
acceptance_tests: defect mapped to exactly one primary category with rationale
ambiguous cases list secondary categories

nodes.definition: Detect and judge attacks on the arguer rather than the argument (abusive, circumstantial, tu quoque), distinguishing fallacious attacks from legitimate relevance to credibility.
contradictors: debater who treats all character reference as fallacy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the attack bears legitimately on testimony credibility

pros.claim: separates irrelevant abuse from relevant credibility challenge
pros.example: attacking a paid lobbyist's bias is relevant; mocking their accent is not

cons.claim: credibility can be genuinely relevant, so blanket labeling overreaches
cons.example: impeaching an eyewitness's eyesight is legitimate, not ad hominem

failure_modes: legitimate bias challenge mislabeled
character attack accepted as refuting the claim
acceptance_tests: the attack is tested for relevance to the claim's truth or the source's credibility
subtype is named

nodes.definition: Diagnose appeals to authority and to emotion, separating fallacious appeals (irrelevant, unqualified, manipulative) from legitimate expert testimony and apt emotional relevance.
contradictors: scientism critic who rejects all expert appeals

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when expert qualification or emotional relevance is re-evaluated

pros.claim: applies Walton's critical questions to keep legitimate appeals usable
pros.example: citing a relevant climate scientist on climate is legitimate appeal to authority

cons.claim: the line depends on expertise relevance and consensus, which can be contested
cons.example: an authority outside their field, or fabricated emotion, makes the appeal fallacious

failure_modes: unqualified celebrity treated as authority
fear appeal substituted for evidence
acceptance_tests: expertise relevance, qualification, and consensus critical questions are checked
emotional content is tested for relevance to the claim

nodes.definition: Detect ambiguity fallacies where a term shifts meaning across the argument (equivocation) or grammatical structure creates ambiguity (amphiboly).
contradictors: literalist who ignores context-fixed meaning

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a term's sense is held fixed or shown to shift

pros.claim: fixing each term to a single sense exposes meaning-shift inferences
pros.example: 'nothing is better than happiness; a sandwich is better than nothing' equivocates on 'nothing'

cons.claim: some apparent equivocations are legitimate context-shifts, not fallacies
cons.example: technical vs ordinary sense used consistently within each premise

failure_modes: term sense shifts undetected
grammatical ambiguity read as a single reading
acceptance_tests: each key term is assigned a single sense and tested for shift across premises
amphibolous sentences are disambiguated before appraisal
revisit_triggers: new parse of an ambiguous sentence

nodes.definition: Detect false dilemmas/dichotomies that present an exhaustive-looking but incomplete set of options, and test whether the disjunction is genuinely exhaustive.
contradictors: forced-choice rhetorician

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a genuinely exhaustive dichotomy is mistaken for a false one

pros.claim: checking exhaustiveness recovers suppressed third options
pros.example: 'either cut taxes or bankrupt the state' ignores spending reform

cons.claim: some dichotomies are genuinely exhaustive (true contradictories)
cons.example: 'either p or not-p' is a real, exhaustive dichotomy

failure_modes: genuine dichotomy mislabeled false
suppressed options not surfaced
acceptance_tests: the disjunction is tested for genuine exhaustiveness
at least one omitted option is named when the dilemma is false

nodes.definition: Detect circular reasoning and question-begging where a premise presupposes or restates the conclusion, leaving the inference epistemically idle.
contradictors: foundationalist who calls all self-support circular

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a premise's independent support is reassessed

pros.claim: detecting premise-conclusion identity exposes epistemically idle inferences
pros.example: 'the Bible is true because it is the word of God, who cannot lie' assumes its conclusion

cons.claim: valid arguments are technically circular, so the test is dialectical not formal
cons.example: every valid argument 'contains' its conclusion; the fault is dialectical uselessness

failure_modes: mutual support mistaken for vicious circularity
hidden equivalence of premise and conclusion missed
acceptance_tests: each premise is checked for independent support from the conclusion
dialectical (not merely formal) circularity is the test applied

nodes.definition: Detect generalizations drawn from samples too small, biased, or unrepresentative to support the universal or statistical conclusion claimed.
contradictors: anecdotalist who universalizes from cases

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when sample size or representativeness data is revised

pros.claim: links the fallacy to sampling adequacy, making it measurable
pros.example: two rude tourists do not show a nation is rude

cons.claim: a small sample can be adequate for a modest or bounded claim
cons.example: one well-chosen case can refute a universal claim

failure_modes: small biased sample universalized
representativeness ignored
acceptance_tests: sample size and representativeness are assessed against the claim's scope
the conclusion's quantifier is matched to the evidence

nodes.definition: Evaluate slippery-slope arguments by testing whether each causal or conceptual step in the chain is independently warranted, distinguishing fallacious from evidence-backed slopes.
contradictors: alarmist who asserts chains without links

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when evidence for a step's probability is added or removed

pros.claim: step-by-step warrant testing separates real risks from scare chains
pros.example: 'legalizing X leads inevitably to Y to Z' fails if no step is supported

cons.claim: some slopes are real when each link has empirical support
cons.example: a documented precedent chain can make a slope argument cogent

failure_modes: unsupported chain accepted as inevitable
each link's probability not multiplied through
acceptance_tests: each step in the chain is tested for independent warrant
the cumulative probability of the full chain is assessed

nodes.definition: Detect misrepresentation of an opponent's position into a weaker form that is then refuted, and contrast it with charitable (steelman) reconstruction.
contradictors: polemicist who refutes caricatures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the original position is restated more accurately

pros.claim: comparing the attacked version to the original exposes distortion
pros.example: refuting 'they want open borders' when they proposed visa reform

cons.claim: a fair restatement can look like distortion if the original was vague
cons.example: clarifying a vague claim is not necessarily a straw man

failure_modes: caricature refuted instead of the real claim
weakest version attacked while strongest ignored
acceptance_tests: the attacked version is compared against the opponent's actual stated position
the strongest available form of the position is addressed

nodes.definition: Screen the reasoner's process for confirmation bias and motivated reasoning that bias premise selection and evidence weighting independent of argument form.
contradictors: pure-logician who ignores reasoning psychology

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the reasoner's motivation or stake in the conclusion changes

pros.claim: flags process-level distortion that form-only analysis misses
pros.example: citing only studies that confirm a prior while ignoring contrary ones

cons.claim: bias attribution is itself bias-prone and hard to verify from text alone
cons.example: accusing an opponent of motivated reasoning can be motivated reasoning

failure_modes: one-sided evidence selection unnoticed
desired conclusion drives premise acceptance
acceptance_tests: evidence selection is checked for asymmetry between confirming and disconfirming sources
a disconfirmation test is proposed

nodes.definition: Detect anchoring and availability heuristics distorting magnitude estimates and probability judgments embedded in an argument's premises.
contradictors: rational-actor theorist who denies systematic bias

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the salient anchor or vivid example driving an estimate is identified

pros.claim: explains why estimates cluster around irrelevant anchors or vivid cases
pros.example: a starting figure pulls an estimate even when admittedly arbitrary

cons.claim: distinguishing a heuristic shortcut from a justified prior is hard
cons.example: an available example may also be genuinely representative

failure_modes: arbitrary anchor drives a premise estimate
vivid-but-rare event overweighted as probable
acceptance_tests: quantitative premises are checked for an arbitrary anchor
probability premises are checked against base rates not availability

nodes.definition: Apply the principle of charity and a steelman pass as a final gate before issuing any fallacy verdict, ensuring the strongest faithful reading was evaluated.
contradictors: adversary who wants the quickest takedown

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a stronger faithful reconstruction reverses a fallacy verdict

pros.claim: a charity gate prevents premature or uncharitable fallacy labels from being finalized
pros.example: reversing an 'equivocation' verdict once a consistent reading is found

cons.claim: excessive charity can immunize bad arguments from any criticism
cons.example: steelmanning into a different, better argument the author never made

failure_modes: fallacy verdict finalized on an uncharitable reading
steelman substitutes a new argument for the original
acceptance_tests: the strongest faithful reconstruction was evaluated before any guilty verdict
each verdict records that charity was applied

edges.why_related: extraction can only proceed once a passage is confirmed to be an argument
edges.benefit_of_coupling: avoids parsing premises out of non-arguments
edges.risk_of_conflict: premise-hunting in an explanation wastes effort
edges.example: an explanatory passage yields no premises to extract
edges.resolution_rule: confirm argumenthood before extraction

edges.why_related: standardization needs the premises and conclusion already labeled
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clean standard form inherits correct labels
edges.risk_of_conflict: reconstructing before extraction misplaces the conclusion
edges.example: standard form built on a mis-labeled conclusion
edges.resolution_rule: extract before standardizing

edges.why_related: the intended inference type is read off the reconstructed argument
edges.benefit_of_coupling: type classification uses a faithful standard form
edges.risk_of_conflict: classifying an un-reconstructed argument misreads intent
edges.example: supplied enthymeme reveals deductive intent
edges.resolution_rule: reconstruct before classifying inference type

edges.why_related: validity appraisal applies only once the argument is typed deductive
edges.benefit_of_coupling: right standard avoids category errors
edges.risk_of_conflict: appraising validity on an inductive argument is a category error
edges.example: a 'must' argument routed to validity testing
edges.resolution_rule: fix inference type before validity appraisal

edges.why_related: form recognition operationalizes the validity verdict
edges.benefit_of_coupling: named forms speed valid/invalid decisions
edges.risk_of_conflict: matching forms before establishing deductive intent misfires
edges.example: modus tollens confirms validity
edges.resolution_rule: establish deductive appraisal before form matching

edges.why_related: strength appraisal applies only to inductively-typed arguments
edges.benefit_of_coupling: correct standard prevents over-harsh deductive judging
edges.risk_of_conflict: judging strength on a deductive argument misapplies the standard
edges.example: a sample-based generalization routed to strength
edges.resolution_rule: type the argument before strength appraisal

edges.why_related: best-explanation appraisal applies to abductively-typed arguments
edges.benefit_of_coupling: explanatory-virtue scoring is used only where apt
edges.risk_of_conflict: scoring virtues on a deductive proof is misplaced
edges.example: an inference-to-best-explanation routed to abductive appraisal
edges.resolution_rule: type the argument before abductive appraisal

edges.why_related: defeasibility judgment presupposes the argument's inferential standing
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scheme matching reuses the inference type
edges.risk_of_conflict: assessing defeasibility before typing confuses standards
edges.example: a presumptive inference flagged for scheme analysis
edges.resolution_rule: type before defeasibility assessment

edges.why_related: category routing follows from the appraisal standard the type sets
edges.benefit_of_coupling: routing inherits the correct appraisal frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: routing before typing risks wrong critical questions
edges.example: an irrelevance defect routed to the relevance category
edges.resolution_rule: type before fallacy routing

edges.why_related: ad hominem diagnosis is reached only after routing to relevance
edges.benefit_of_coupling: specific diagnosis inherits the relevance frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: diagnosing ad hominem outside the relevance route mislabels
edges.example: a personal attack routed to relevance then to ad hominem
edges.resolution_rule: route to category before naming the fallacy

edges.why_related: appeal diagnosis is reached after routing to relevance
edges.benefit_of_coupling: appeal critical questions inherit the relevance frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: diagnosing an appeal outside the route misfires
edges.example: an expert citation routed to relevance
edges.resolution_rule: route before appeal diagnosis

edges.why_related: ambiguity diagnosis follows routing to the ambiguity category
edges.benefit_of_coupling: term-sense analysis inherits the ambiguity frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing for equivocation off-route wastes effort
edges.example: a meaning-shift defect routed to ambiguity
edges.resolution_rule: route before ambiguity diagnosis

edges.why_related: false-dilemma diagnosis follows routing to presumption
edges.benefit_of_coupling: exhaustiveness test inherits the presumption frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing dichotomies off-route misfires
edges.example: a forced-choice defect routed to presumption
edges.resolution_rule: route before false-dilemma diagnosis

edges.why_related: circularity diagnosis follows routing to presumption
edges.benefit_of_coupling: dependency check inherits the presumption frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing circularity off-route misfires
edges.example: a self-supporting premise routed to presumption
edges.resolution_rule: route before begging-the-question diagnosis

edges.why_related: hasty-generalization diagnosis follows routing to presumption
edges.benefit_of_coupling: sample-adequacy test inherits the presumption frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing generalizations off-route misfires
edges.example: a small-sample claim routed to presumption
edges.resolution_rule: route before hasty-generalization diagnosis

edges.why_related: slope diagnosis follows routing to presumption
edges.benefit_of_coupling: per-step warrant test inherits the presumption frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing slopes off-route misfires
edges.example: a consequence-chain claim routed to presumption
edges.resolution_rule: route before slippery-slope diagnosis

edges.why_related: straw-man diagnosis follows routing to presumption/distortion
edges.benefit_of_coupling: distortion comparison inherits the frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing for straw man off-route misfires
edges.example: a misrepresentation routed to distortion
edges.resolution_rule: route before straw-man diagnosis

edges.why_related: straw-man detection compares the attack to a faithful reconstruction of the original
edges.benefit_of_coupling: faithful original enables distortion detection
edges.risk_of_conflict: without reconstruction the 'original' is itself a guess
edges.example: comparing the attack to a charitable restatement
edges.resolution_rule: reconstruct the target position before straw-man diagnosis

edges.why_related: hasty generalization is the failure case of inductive strength on samples
edges.benefit_of_coupling: sample-adequacy criteria are shared
edges.risk_of_conflict: diagnosing the fallacy without strength criteria is ad hoc
edges.example: an under-sampled generalization fails the strength test
edges.resolution_rule: apply strength criteria when diagnosing hasty generalization

edges.why_related: a defeasibility check should precede finalizing an ad hominem charge
edges.benefit_of_coupling: avoids labeling relevant credibility challenges as fallacies
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping it over-diagnoses ad hominem
edges.example: a bias-relevant attack cleared by critical questions
edges.resolution_rule: run defeasibility before finalizing the relevance verdict

edges.why_related: a defeasibility check should precede finalizing an appeal charge
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keeps legitimate expert/emotion appeals usable
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping it over-diagnoses appeals
edges.example: a qualified-expert appeal cleared by critical questions
edges.resolution_rule: run defeasibility before finalizing the appeal verdict

edges.why_related: evidence-backed slopes should survive a defeasibility check
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keeps cogent precedent-chain arguments valid
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping it over-diagnoses slopes
edges.example: a documented slope cleared as cogent
edges.resolution_rule: run defeasibility before finalizing the slope verdict

edges.why_related: the final gate consumes defeasibility results to adjudicate verdicts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: verdicts inherit critical-question outcomes
edges.risk_of_conflict: gating without defeasibility finalizes brittle verdicts
edges.example: an unanswered critical question blocks a not-guilty verdict
edges.resolution_rule: complete defeasibility before the verdict gate

edges.why_related: the gate adjudicates the ad hominem verdict under charity
edges.benefit_of_coupling: final verdict is charity-checked
edges.risk_of_conflict: finalizing before the gate risks uncharitable labels
edges.example: an ad hominem verdict reversed after a charitable reading
edges.resolution_rule: pass diagnoses through the charity gate

edges.why_related: straw-man and charity are two sides of faithful representation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the gate enforces steelman before a guilty verdict
edges.risk_of_conflict: finalizing a straw-man charge without steelman is premature
edges.example: a distortion verdict held until the strongest reading is tested
edges.resolution_rule: pass straw-man diagnoses through the charity gate

edges.why_related: process-level bias screening attaches once the argument is typed and reconstructed
edges.benefit_of_coupling: bias flags target the right premises
edges.risk_of_conflict: screening before reconstruction targets noise
edges.example: confirmation bias flagged in premise selection
edges.resolution_rule: type and reconstruct before bias screening

edges.why_related: estimate-bias screening attaches to typed quantitative premises
edges.benefit_of_coupling: anchor/availability flags target real estimates
edges.risk_of_conflict: screening before typing misallocates effort
edges.example: an anchored magnitude estimate flagged
edges.resolution_rule: type before estimate-bias screening

edges.why_related: both screen reasoning-process biases rather than argument form
edges.benefit_of_coupling: shared debiasing toolkit
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them blurs distinct mechanisms
edges.example: confirmation bias vs anchoring are distinct biases
edges.resolution_rule: treat as related but distinct bias screens

edges.why_related: maximal charity can convert a fair straw-man charge into an unwarranted rescue of a bad argument
edges.benefit_of_coupling: forces a principled charity ceiling
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-charity immunizes distortions from critique
edges.example: steelmanning into an argument the author never made
edges.resolution_rule: cap charity at the strongest FAITHFUL reading; do not substitute a new argument

edges.why_related: context-sensitive defeasibility resists the clean category labels routing wants
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balances nuance against tractable diagnosis
edges.risk_of_conflict: pure form-routing over-diagnoses; pure defeasibility under-diagnoses
edges.example: a textbook 'fallacy' that is reasonable in its dialogue type
edges.resolution_rule: route by category but let defeasibility override the final label

edges.why_related: applying deductive validity to inductive arguments (or vice versa) creates a standards clash
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keeps each standard in its lane
edges.risk_of_conflict: cross-applying standards yields category errors
edges.example: calling a strong induction 'invalid'
edges.resolution_rule: apply the standard fixed by INFERENCE_TYPE_CLASS, never the other

edges.why_related: process-bias suspicion can wrongly discredit a formally valid argument
edges.benefit_of_coupling: separates ad hominem-on-process from logic
edges.risk_of_conflict: biasing the verdict by the arguer's motives is itself fallacious
edges.example: dismissing a valid proof because the prover is biased
edges.resolution_rule: judge the argument on form; treat bias only as a process caution

edges.why_related: charity to the arguer tensions against flagging their motivated reasoning
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balances fairness with bias vigilance
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-charity hides motivated reasoning; over-screening becomes ad hominem
edges.example: excusing cherry-picked evidence as good-faith emphasis
edges.resolution_rule: apply charity to the argument's content, bias screening to the process

conflict_axes.trigger: maximizing charity tensions against issuing a deserved fallacy verdict
resolution_order: fix the strongest FAITHFUL reading
evaluate that reading
issue a verdict only if it still fails
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: charity is capped at the strongest reading the author actually intended; it never substitutes a new argument
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if charity would rewrite the thesis into a different argument
conflict_axes.example: steelmanning a vague claim into a sound one the author never made

conflict_axes.trigger: a form-based fallacy label conflicts with a context that licenses the move
resolution_order: route by category for a candidate label
run the scheme's critical questions
let context override the label
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: context-sensitive defeasibility overrides a form-only label when the relevant critical questions are answered
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a textbook fallacy is reasonable in its dialogue type
conflict_axes.example: an appeal to authority that passes all critical questions

conflict_axes.trigger: the wrong appraisal standard is applied to the argument's intended type
resolution_order: confirm the inference type
apply only the matching standard
report the other only as inapplicable
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the standard fixed by INFERENCE_TYPE_CLASS dominates; cross-applying validity to induction (or vice versa) is rejected
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a strong induction is judged 'invalid' or a deduction judged 'weak'
conflict_axes.example: calling 'most A are B; x is A; so x is B' invalid

conflict_axes.trigger: suspicion of motivated reasoning pressures dismissing a formally good argument
resolution_order: judge the argument on its merits
record bias only as a process caution
never let motive decide the logical verdict
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: argument form dominates the truth verdict; bias screening informs scrutiny but does not refute a valid argument
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if an argument is rejected solely because the arguer is biased
conflict_axes.example: dismissing a valid proof because the prover has a stake

conflict_axes.trigger: a binary framing may be a false dilemma or a practically adequate simplification
resolution_order: test the disjunction for genuine exhaustiveness
weigh practical relevance of omitted options
label false only if a relevant option is suppressed
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: genuine non-exhaustiveness with a relevant omitted option dominates toward a false-dilemma verdict; otherwise the simplification stands
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a real, decision-relevant third option is suppressed
conflict_axes.example: 'comply or quit' when negotiation is a live option

conflict_axes.trigger: full critical-question and charity passes cost time that fast labeling skips
resolution_order: triage by stakes of the verdict
apply deep analysis to high-stakes or contested arguments
fast-label only low-stakes clear cases
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for high-risk or contested verdicts, depth dominates speed; for low-stakes clear cases, throughput is acceptable
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a high-stakes verdict is issued without the charity gate
conflict_axes.example: mass-labeling debate transcripts without critical questions

conflict_axes.trigger: aggressive detection raises false positives while caution misses real fallacies
resolution_order: set a detection threshold by stakes
require a named scheme failure for a positive
accept misses on borderline reasonable moves
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for accusation-grade verdicts, precision dominates (require a clear scheme failure); for screening, recall may dominate
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if borderline presumptive inferences are routinely labeled fallacies
conflict_axes.example: flagging every expert citation as appeal to authority

conflict_axes.trigger: a term used in a technical sense can look like equivocation against ordinary usage
resolution_order: fix the author's intended sense per premise
check for an actual shift across premises
label equivocation only on a genuine shift
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: a genuine cross-premise sense shift dominates toward an equivocation verdict; consistent technical usage does not
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if ordinary-sense reading is imposed on a defined technical term
conflict_axes.example: reading 'work' in physics as the everyday sense

edge_cases.trigger: a non-argument is processed as an argument
edge_cases.failure_mode: fabricated premises and a phantom fallacy
edge_cases.example: reading a list of facts as if it argued for one of them
edge_cases.detection_method: apply the inference-claim test before extraction

edge_cases.trigger: an argument is appraised by the standard for the wrong inference type
edge_cases.failure_mode: category-error verdict (e.g., strong induction called invalid)
edge_cases.detection_method: check that the appraisal node matches INFERENCE_TYPE_CLASS output

edge_cases.trigger: a fallacy verdict is finalized on an uncharitable reading
edge_cases.failure_mode: unjust fallacy attribution; self straw man
edge_cases.example: declaring equivocation before trying a consistent reading
edge_cases.detection_method: verify the charity gate ran and recorded the strongest faithful reading

edge_cases.trigger: excessive charity rebuilds a new, better argument the author never made
edge_cases.failure_mode: bad arguments immunized from valid critique
edge_cases.example: steelmanning a vague slogan into a rigorous thesis
edge_cases.detection_method: check that supplied premises trace to author intent, not the analyst's improvement

edge_cases.trigger: concluding a claim is false because its argument is fallacious
edge_cases.example: 'your reasoning is fallacious, therefore your conclusion is false'
edge_cases.detection_method: check that the verdict targets the inference, not the truth of the conclusion
resolution: restrict the verdict to the inference
note the conclusion may still be true

edge_cases.trigger: a legitimate presumptive inference is labeled a fallacy by form alone
edge_cases.example: flagging a qualified expert appeal as appeal-to-authority fallacy
edge_cases.detection_method: require the scheme's critical questions to fail before a positive verdict

edge_cases.trigger: a key term shifts sense undetected during standardization
edge_cases.failure_mode: invalid inference masked by a single token
edge_cases.example: 'nothing is better than X; Y is better than nothing'
edge_cases.detection_method: assign each key term one sense and test for cross-premise shift

edge_cases.trigger: the conclusion's quantifier exceeds what the sample supports
edge_cases.failure_mode: unsupported universal from a small sample
edge_cases.example: 'all' concluded from a handful of cases
edge_cases.detection_method: match the conclusion quantifier to sample size and representativeness

edge_cases.trigger: a bias flag is used to refute a formally valid argument
edge_cases.failure_mode: ad hominem-by-bias; valid argument wrongly dismissed
edge_cases.example: rejecting a valid proof because the prover is motivated
edge_cases.detection_method: ensure bias flags inform scrutiny only, never the truth verdict

edge_cases.trigger: a consequence chain is accepted without per-step warrant
edge_cases.example: 'X leads inevitably to catastrophe' with no link evidence
edge_cases.detection_method: test each step for independent warrant and multiply probabilities
resolution: downgrade to weak if any link unsupported

edge_cases.trigger: derived metric fields do not match the formula inputs
edge_cases.example: a hand-edited final_importance not matching its inputs
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute all derived fields with the formula tool and compare within 0.02

edge_cases.trigger: template placeholder text survives into the populated KB
edge_cases.example: a residual unfilled template token or example-id string survives
edge_cases.detection_method: scan for the known placeholder set before finalizing

workflow.objective: confirm an argument is present and extract its premises and conclusion
acceptance_tests: passage confirmed to make an inferential claim
premises and conclusion labeled
workflow.do_first_because: no appraisal is meaningful until the argument and its parts are fixed

workflow.objective: standardize the argument and charitably supply intended premises
acceptance_tests: standard form preserves the original conclusion
each supplied premise is justified
workflow.do_first_because: a faithful standard form prevents downstream straw-man and mislabeling

workflow.objective: classify the intended inference type and select the appraisal standard
acceptance_tests: inference type stated with its cue
appraisal standard matches the type
workflow.do_first_because: the appraisal standard set here scopes all subsequent appraisal and routing

workflow.objective: appraise validity, soundness, and named forms for deductive arguments
acceptance_tests: a counterexample is sought for any claimed-valid form
validity and soundness reported separately
workflow.do_first_because: deductive appraisal is form-decidable and anchors the verdict for demonstrative arguments

workflow.objective: appraise strength/cogency and best-explanation quality for non-deductive arguments
acceptance_tests: strength rated on evidence not certainty
at least one rival hypothesis compared
workflow.do_first_because: non-demonstrative arguments need degree-based standards distinct from validity

workflow.objective: route any defect to its category and assess whether it is a reasonable defeasible move
entry_criteria: an appraisal flagged a candidate defect
acceptance_tests: defect mapped to one primary category
scheme critical questions identified
workflow.do_first_because: category-first routing prevents wrong critical questions and over-diagnosis

workflow.objective: diagnose relevance and ambiguity fallacies with their critical questions
entry_criteria: category routed to relevance or ambiguity
acceptance_tests: each appeal/attack tested for genuine relevance
each key term fixed to one sense
workflow.do_first_because: these diagnoses share the routing frame and can run before final adjudication

entry_criteria: category routed to presumption or distortion
acceptance_tests: each disjunction tested for exhaustiveness
samples assessed against claim scope
chains tested per step
workflow.do_first_because: presumption fallacies require their own warrant tests before adjudication

workflow.objective: screen the reasoning process for cognitive biases independent of form
entry_criteria: the argument and its evidence base are reconstructed
acceptance_tests: evidence selection checked for confirmation asymmetry
estimates checked against anchors and base rates
workflow.do_first_because: process-bias cautions inform scrutiny but must not decide the logical verdict

workflow.objective: apply the charity gate and issue final adjudicated verdicts
entry_criteria: all candidate verdicts and defeasibility results are available
acceptance_tests: the strongest faithful reading was evaluated before any guilty verdict
each verdict records charity application
workflow.do_first_because: the charity gate is the last anti-rework guard against premature or unjust verdicts

priority_rationale.notes: root: gates whether any extraction or appraisal applies
faithful standard form prevents downstream mislabeling
sets the appraisal standard scoping all later work
defeasibility gates over-diagnosis across all fallacy nodes
routes defects to the correct critical questions
distortion check tied to faithful reconstruction
relevance fallacy diagnosis with critical questions
final verdict gate; charity adjudication before lock

dominance_rules.trigger: a fallacy verdict is about to be issued on an uncharitable reading
dominance_rules.rule: the strongest faithful reading dominates a quick takedown
dominance_rules.required_action: evaluate the steelman before any guilty verdict
dominance_rules.example: reverse an equivocation charge once a consistent reading is found

dominance_rules.trigger: the appraisal standard does not match the inference type
dominance_rules.rule: the standard fixed by inference type dominates
dominance_rules.required_action: apply only the matching appraisal standard
dominance_rules.example: do not call a strong induction invalid

dominance_rules.trigger: a form-based fallacy label conflicts with a context that licenses the move
dominance_rules.rule: answered critical questions dominate a form-only label
dominance_rules.required_action: let defeasibility override the label when critical questions pass
dominance_rules.example: clear a qualified-expert appeal that passes its critical questions

dominance_rules.trigger: an argument is being rejected because the arguer is biased
dominance_rules.rule: argument form dominates the truth verdict over arguer motive
dominance_rules.required_action: judge the argument on its merits and treat bias as a caution only
dominance_rules.example: do not dismiss a valid proof for the prover's stake

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-stakes verdict is about to skip the charity or critical-question pass
dominance_rules.rule: verdict correctness dominates diagnostic speed for high-stakes cases
dominance_rules.required_action: require the full pass before an accusation-grade verdict
dominance_rules.example: no public fallacy charge without the charity gate

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value diagnosis is attempted before its prerequisite is fixed
dominance_rules.required_action: complete the prerequisite node before the dependent one
dominance_rules.example: do not diagnose ad hominem before routing to relevance

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible verdict is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automated acceptance for high-risk verdicts
dominance_rules.required_action: route the verdict to human review before lock
dominance_rules.example: an accusation of bad faith requires human sign-off

dominance_rules.trigger: numeric scores are presented without eligible evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: label all estimates heuristic absent eligible data
dominance_rules.example: do not label a guessed detection rate as observed

dominance_rules.trigger: a verdict is about to be locked before validation passes
dominance_rules.required_action: block hard lock until charity, critical-question, and formula gates pass
dominance_rules.example: no verdict lock before the charity record is complete

dominance_rules.trigger: a borderline presumptive inference is about to be labeled a fallacy
dominance_rules.rule: for accusation-grade verdicts, precision dominates recall
dominance_rules.required_action: require a named scheme failure before a positive verdict
dominance_rules.example: do not flag every expert citation as a fallacy

dominance_rules.trigger: charity would rewrite the thesis into a different argument
dominance_rules.required_action: cap charity at the strongest reading the author intended
dominance_rules.example: do not steelman a slogan into a thesis the author never made

dominance_rules.trigger: a verdict or object is added without traceability to a question or source
dominance_rules.required_action: link each verdict to a competency question and source
dominance_rules.example: drop a diagnosis that answers no stated competency question

anti_rework_rules.rule: confirm a passage is an argument before extracting premises
anti_rework_rules.rationale: extracting premises from a non-argument wastes the whole analysis
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: premise list built for an explanatory passage

anti_rework_rules.rule: label premises and conclusion before standardizing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: standardizing a mis-labeled argument propagates the error
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: standard form with the wrong main conclusion
anti_rework_rules.example: reconstructing before the conclusion is fixed

anti_rework_rules.rule: produce a faithful standard form before typing the inference
anti_rework_rules.rationale: typing an un-reconstructed argument misreads intended strength
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: type assigned from rhetorical surface, not structure
anti_rework_rules.example: calling an enthymeme inductive before supplying its universal premise

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the inference type before applying any appraisal standard
anti_rework_rules.rationale: appraising before typing causes category errors and rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: validity test run on an inductive argument

anti_rework_rules.rule: route a defect to its category before naming a specific fallacy
anti_rework_rules.rationale: naming before routing applies the wrong critical questions
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a fallacy named with no category rationale
anti_rework_rules.example: calling a move 'ad hominem' without the relevance route

anti_rework_rules.rule: run the defeasibility check before finalizing a fallacy verdict
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a guilty verdict with no critical-question record
anti_rework_rules.example: labeling an evidence-backed slope a fallacy

anti_rework_rules.rule: reconstruct the target position before charging straw man
anti_rework_rules.rationale: without a faithful original the straw-man charge is itself a guess
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: straw-man verdict with no cited original
anti_rework_rules.example: comparing an attack to an un-reconstructed position

anti_rework_rules.rule: apply the charity gate before locking any verdict
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking before charity risks unjust, hard-to-reverse verdicts
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: verdict locked with no charity-compliance record
anti_rework_rules.example: publishing a fallacy charge before steelmanning

anti_rework_rules.rule: populate base metric inputs before computing derived scores
anti_rework_rules.rationale: computing scores before inputs yields formula inconsistency
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: derived fields edited without their inputs

anti_rework_rules.rule: re-run validation after every material repair
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unvalidated repairs can introduce new failures
anti_rework_rules.example: fixing an edge reference but not re-checking acyclicity

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem
high-risk defects scheduled first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only low-risk below tolerance

iteration_protocol.detection: trace edges from the changed node
acceptance_tests: all downstream dependents identified

iteration_protocol.detection: map defect type to owner via repair_routing
acceptance_tests: defect routed to a valid owner

iteration_protocol.detection: recompute derived fields and re-run the validator
acceptance_tests: no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence about a diagnosis arrives
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed within tolerance

iteration_protocol.trigger: a dependency cycle or invalid edge is detected
acceptance_tests: dependency graph acyclic
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no cycles and all endpoints valid

iteration_protocol.trigger: a verdict is contested on charity grounds
acceptance_tests: strongest faithful reading evaluated

acceptance_tests: no validity regression versus baseline
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no regression or accepted with record
